description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotional categories in a dataset used for evaluating speaker anonymization on emotional speech, with six distinct emotion labels represented as colored segments. The largest segment, labeled “Frustration,” occupies 25.1% of the chart and is colored light blue. The second largest, “Neutral,” accounts for 23.1% and is shown in dark blue. “Excitement” follows at 14.1% in red, while “Sadness” comprises 14.7% in orange. “Anger” is represented by a yellow segment at 14.9%, and the smallest segment, “Happiness,” makes up 8.1% and is colored light purple. Each slice is clearly labeled with its emotion and percentage value, and the chart uses a standard circular layout with no exploded segments or additional annotations beyond the labels and values. The distribution suggests a relatively balanced spread across most emotions, with “Frustration” and “Neutral” being the most prevalent.
